dharmatiles · visual review · type, colour, layout, icons, motion, the 3D view · 14 Nov 2026

The plate and
the meadow

The site already knows what dharmatiles looks like: a pale ruled plate with a tile on it, under quiet chrome. The editor stage does not. This review says what I would make from nothing, and what I would change in what is there.

Thesis

Make the plate the only stage. If I started today I would build one idea and repeat it: a quiet, nearly colourless instrument, with all colour belonging to the model. The tile sits on a plate (the ruled #D9E0EB slab you already render on), the plate sits on the chrome, and nothing else in the interface competes with the terrain. Red and orange stay reserved for overhang because nothing else is loud.

You are closer to that than most projects. The type trio, the lotus, the square status marks, the four sizes, the no-pill corners and the two themes are right, and I would not touch them. The distance that is left is concentrated in four places: the stage (meadow, not plate), messages (five different looks for one thing), live cards (states that read as separate widgets), and the panel order (print admin above the stack you came to edit).

Keep. Big Shoulders for names, Plex for reading, JetBrains Mono only for what you type.
Keep. Lichen & Linen and Moonpool, with one accent that means "you can press this".
Keep. Square 8 px status marks, sentence-case labels, two control heights, one icon set.
Keep. Red and orange for overhang only; --err as a separate token.
What I saw and what I did not. I ran the editor from a scratch home at 1440 and 400 px, light and dark, and the site locally and live. This checkout has no docs/posters/ (they are made at deploy), so local live cards show a broken poster, and the live site has not yet shipped the cards or the playground (404). The live-card states below come from screenshots left in the shared scratchpad by an earlier session, same code, taken this morning. I did not run the CLI, and I did not see a tile that fails the overhang gate; the overhang points are reasoning from the colours, marked as such.

Findings, by what you see first

1 · the editor stage

The stage is a meadow, so the plate rule is not true in the editor

visual-system.html says the preview's stage is the plate with the tile's own grid. What renders is a grass field with a dark blotch pattern (light) or a dark green-black grid (dark). Three consequences:

  • Grass, water+grass and tree tiles are green on green. The tile edge is carried by its shadow alone.
  • When nothing is built (empty, error, loading) the stage is a flat slate blue, #5F7387-ish, which is neither plate nor meadow. It is the first thing a new user sees.
  • A 6 px black bar runs down the left edge of the stage in every empty or error shot (see the first two screenshots below). It looks like a mis-sized canvas.
ChangeA finite plate, about 3 squares larger than the tile on each side, ruled in the tile's own 35 mm squares, with a soft contact shadow. Beyond it the stage is the chrome's own background colour. Empty state shows the bare plate with the "Make terrain" card on it. The same plate in both themes, as the rule says.
2 · messages

One mistake is drawn five ways

The same dt:: error appears as: a large red-titled card in the outline; a second card on the stage with a different title ("Nothing built") and the same words, at once; a wavy underline across the whole source line; an unstyled paragraph block inside a live card (copy icon wrapped onto its own line, no code chip, no hierarchy); and an overflowing red box in the playground whose URL does not wrap, with a broken-image alt text under it.

The source underline covers grass at=bnk; the mistake is bnk. The span exists (the error says "line 20"); the mark does not use it.

ChangeOne message anatomy, drawn by one component everywhere: code, one sentence, the offending source with the span underlined, one primary fix button, then secondary links. The stage never repeats it; on error the stage keeps the last good build, dimmed 40%, with a small "last good build" chip at its corner. Error pages with live cards (Phase 3½) reuse the same component.
dt::atNo place is called bnk. Did you mean bank? stack { … grass at=bnk }Change to bankExplainGo to line

Mock-up. Red here is --err, the interface's danger red, and appears only on the code and the underline, never as a fill.

3 · live examples on a page

A card's states read as different widgets, and a page of them is long

Cold, the card is lovely: a painted poster, one small button, the source beside it. Awake, it becomes a five-group stack (toggle chips, sliders, a source box, four buttons, a status strip, then the message). Draft detail is a flat triangulated render in blue, white and brown that looks like a fault next to the poster; the only label is a line of text under everything, after the render.

On a phone the poster alone is a 370 px square, then the source, then controls: one card is roughly two screens. A page with six of them is twelve.

The engine can hold one WebGL context at a time, so the others fall back to poster. That is the right behaviour, but nothing on a poster says "you can touch this", and nothing says which card is awake.

ChangeOne card, one state machine, drawn in one place: asleep (poster, a small play glyph that is also the "Edit this example" button), waking (the poster stays, a 2 px accent progress rule runs along the poster's foot), draft (same materials, lower resolution, a "draft" chip on the render's corner), full (chip gone, 200 ms crossfade, nothing else changes), failed (last good frame dimmed, the message component). The awake card gets a 2 px accent outline; its neighbours stay posters. Controls collapse to what that example is about (one slider for wobble, not every layer toggle); on a phone, source goes behind a Source / Controls segmented control under the render.
▶ edit
asleepposter; the glyph says it moves
wakingposter held, progress along its foot

draftsame colours, coarser mesh, chip on the render

The chip is laid on the plate in the plate's own light colours, as the visual-system page already says of anything laid over it.

4 · panel order

The outline opens with print admin; the stack starts at 500 px

At 1440 × 900 the tile outline shows, in order: size, seed, description, Inventory (with its own two-way toggle), Print list (a select and a button), and then Stack, whose first row sits at y ≈ 580. The stack is what the editor is for. Inventory and print list are bookkeeping about a tile that is already done.

Switching to Map or Plates leaves the previous tile standing on the stage behind a list of tiles; the list's thumbnails are empty pale squares until built. The stage reads as "this is the thing" when it is not.

ChangeSize, seed, description (one line each, collapsible), then Stack, then Shape, then a closing "Printing" group holding inventory and print list. In Map and Plates, clear the stage to the bare plate (or show the map). A thumbnail that is not built shows the plate with the tile's footprint outline, not a blank square.
5 · site frame

Thirteen nav items will not take fourteen more pages

The header is one row: Language, Elements, Composing, Preview, Plates, Maps, Printers, Inventory, Tile system, Printing, Rules, Roadmap, Changelog. On a phone it scrolls sideways after "Plates" with no cue that more exists. Phase 1 adds about fourteen concept pages that need a home.

The home hero code is clipped on the right at laptop width (a through line stops mid-point). Code is the argument on that page; clipping it mid-statement is the wrong place to economise. On element pages about 180 px to the right of the contents list is empty, and the element picture (water) is an abstract blue-and-white field that does not say "water" to a stranger; I flag that as a render question for your later pass.

ChangeFour groups: Learn (tour, concepts), Reference (language, elements, cheat sheet, errors), Use (preview, plates, maps, printers, inventory, printing), About (tile system, rules, roadmap, changelog). On a phone, a single "Menu" button opening a sheet. Hero code gets a soft wrap with a hanging indent, as the editor's source already does.
6 · overhang paint (not yet seen failing)

Dirt is the colour of the warning

The cliff render's dirt is a saturated terracotta, close in hue to --band (#FF8C1A) and not far from --over. On a tile with a band patch over dirt, orange on orange-brown may not stand out. I did not have a failing tile to test, so this is a prediction; it is the first thing I would check.

ChangeAn overhang lens: when the gate reports any band or red area, the model drops to a desaturated grey and the paint is the only colour, with a legend chip that gives area per band. Normal view stays as is. Test with a tile that deliberately fails, over dirt, rock and grass.
7 · smaller things

What else I would fix in passing

  • Material swatches in dark. --water #83A8FF and --stone #B9C9CD do not match the teal water and grey-blue rock in the render. Shift dark --water toward teal (about #6FC2CC) so the row and the render agree.
  • Top bar. "saved" floats as bare text between the mode switch and Undo. Make it a status mark and word on the right with the printer chip, where the eye already goes for state.
  • Panel width. 440 px wraps source at about 40 characters. Default to 520 px at 1440 and above; the wrap with hanging indent is already good.
  • Motion. The rule says nothing moves by itself. A build that answers an action may settle: tile 6 px high to resting over 180 ms, with its shadow tightening. That is the one orchestrated moment I would allow, off under reduced motion.
  • CLI. Not reviewed in use. Whatever it prints for a dt:: code should be the message anatomy above in text: code, sentence, source line with carets under the span, one suggested fix, the explain command.

Phases

Each one ships alone. Order is by how much of the first impression it changes per day of work.

A

The plate stage

Finite ruled plate with contact shadow on the chrome's own background. Remove the meadow, the slate-blue empty state and the black bar. Clear the stage in Map and Plates. Unbuilt thumbnails show footprints.

DONE WHENEight screenshots (grass, water+grass, cliff, empty, error, loading; light and dark) show the tile edge separated from the stage at 3:1 luminance; no pixel of the stage is neither plate nor chrome; Map and Plates show no stale model.
B

One message

A single component (editor outline, source, live card, playground, error pages, CLI text). Underline the span, not the line. Stage keeps the last good build, dimmed.

DONE WHENA grep finds one message renderer per surface family; a test with a long URL shows no overflow at 400 px; the stage never repeats the outline's text.
C

One card

The five-state card, one awake at a time, accent outline on the awake one, draft chip, crossfade, collapsed controls, Source / Controls on a phone.

DONE WHENA page with six cards, on a laptop and at 400 px, shows exactly one awake; draft and full use the same palette; a phone card is no taller than one and a half screens; reduced motion removes the crossfade and the settle.
D

Panel order and top bar

Stack first, printing last, one-line description, status mark by the printer chip, 520 px panel on wide screens.

DONE WHENAt 1440 × 900 the first stack row is above y = 300 and the panel's first screen shows at least four stack rows.
E

Site frame

Four nav groups and a phone menu sheet, wrapped hero code, the cheat-sheet and concept pages slotted into Learn and Reference, dark swatch tokens matched to the render.

DONE WHENEvery page is reachable from the phone menu in two taps; no page body scrolls sideways; the dark water and stone swatches are within a visible step of the render's colours.
F

Overhang lens

Build a tile that fails on purpose, over dirt, rock and grass. Add the grey lens and the legend chip with area per band.

DONE WHENOn that tile, band and red patches are identifiable at a glance on all three materials in both themes, with the legend numbers equal to the gate's.

Decisions for Shawn

Is the stage a plate, with nothing beyond it?

The written rule says yes; the editor says meadow. If you like the meadow, the rule is what must change.

RECOMMEND · YES, FINITE PLATEIt matches the rule and the site, fixes green-on-green, and gives the empty and error states a real surface. In dark theme the plate stays light (it is the same in both themes) but small enough that it reads as an object, not a glare.
Keep the meadow as an optional "scenery" setting?
RECOMMEND · NOA setting is a second path. If a sky is wanted later, it is a render for the docs, not a stage.
May the stage dim the last good build on error?

Today an error leaves the stage empty.

RECOMMEND · YESIt answers "what did I just break?" faster than a message. It is not a fallback that changes output: the chip says it is the previous build and nothing is exported from it.
How many live cards awake at once?
RECOMMEND · ONEIt matches the engine's real limit, saves phone battery, and makes the awake card obvious. Put it back to sleep when scrolled out of view.
How should draft detail look?
RECOMMEND · SAME PALETTE, COARSER MESH, CHIPDraft is a speed setting, not a different style. If it must stay faceted, the chip is mandatory.
Four nav groups and a phone menu sheet?

Changes Phase 1's information architecture, so it is worth settling before the concept pages land.

RECOMMEND · YESLearn, Reference, Use, About. Without it, fourteen new pages go into a header that already scrolls on a phone.
Stack before print admin in the outline?
RECOMMEND · YESThe stack is the work. Printing is what happens after.
Dark-theme water and stone swatches: match the render?

The rule says a family has one colour everywhere. Today it has two.

RECOMMEND · YESShift the dark tokens toward the render; keep the hue family so the rule holds.
An overhang lens that greys the model?

Argued from colour alone; a failing tile should confirm or kill it first.

RECOMMEND · YES, AFTER PHASE F'S TEST TILEIf the test shows orange on dirt reads fine, drop the lens and keep the legend.
